state.current_rule: A reviewer approves one exact boundary draft revision, and must not have authored any revision in that entire draft unless a waiver covers the reviewer. The revision includes all scope decisions in the draft.
state.candidate_a: Each scope decision is independently authored and approved by a reviewer who did not author that decision. There is no approval by a single reviewer of the entire exact draft.
state.candidate_b: A reviewer may approve an exact whole draft only after checking every scope decision and every draft author. The check is implemented by following a chain of bounded window records and reading every relevant child fact.
state.requirement: No write decision may depend on examining or managing all children. Reads and reports can page through independently owned records.

whole_scan_write.instructions: Does candidate B make the whole-draft approval write decision depend on checking all scope decisions?

ledger_smell.instructions: Does splitting the chain in candidate B into small windows avoid the requirement to check every decision before approval?

review_semantics.instructions: Is candidate A equivalent to the current rule requiring one reviewer who authored none of the entire draft?

independent_owner.instructions: Can each scope decision enforce its own author-review separation without checking the other scope decisions?

read_only.instructions: Can a read-only report page over many independently approved decisions without making its assembly a write decision?
